source: QZ issue attachments; physical Android HCI captures of one Tacx Neo 2

why: The existing fec_tacx_neo_2 corpus explicitly excludes application transmit lines, so FitBridge
has had no FE-C CONTROL corpus from any device. These captures are one SIM/grade session and one
They also carry a framing defect worth more than the frames themselves - see checksum below.

checksum.antStandardRule: XOR of every octet from SYNC through the last data octet, compared against the trailing octet. This is the rule every RECEIVED frame in fec_tacx_neo_2.json satisfies, and the rule FeCBleControlDecoder enforces.
checksum.observedRule: sum(octets[1..10]) mod 256 - an ADDITIVE checksum that excludes the SYNC octet AND excludes the final data octet
checksum.finding: Not one of the frames carries a valid ANT checksum, and all of them fit the additive rule exactly. Excluding the final data octet is what identifies it as a defect rather than an alternative convention: for page 0x31 the excluded octet is the target-power high byte, so two commands 256 quarter-watts apart produce the same checksum.
checksum.hardwareBehaviour: The trainer honoured them anyway. See ergTargetCorrelation: measured instantaneous power tracks a thirteen-step ERG ladder from 92 W to 174 W within a few watts. A Tacx Neo 2 does NOT validate the ANT checksum on FE-C control writes.
checksum.implicationForFitBridge: FeCBleControlDecoder rejects a mismatched checksum with RejectReason.BAD_CHECKSUM, so every frame in this corpus would be refused by the FitBridge FE-C simulator while real hardware accepts it. That is a strictness gap between the simulator and the machine it emulates, and it is the shape of defect that surfaces to a user as 'the app does not control the trainer' with no diagnosable cause. This fixture does not decide whether to loosen it; it makes the gap executable.
checksum.implicationForFitBridgeCentral: None. FitBridge emits the standard XOR when it writes, which is correct and which this trainer also accepts.

ergTargetCorrelation.note: Measured power is CPS 0x2A63 instantaneous power from the same session; window is 5-25 s after each target change.

unresolvedPage.note: Present in both sessions and in the existing notification corpus. Payload is 0xFC then 00 00 64 00 00 <varying> 00. NOT decoded and deliberately not guessed. Retained as opaque so a future resolution has vectors.

expectations: Raw replay corpus. Decode with the FE-C specification and the production codec; the checksum fields are golden and are the point of the fixture.
privacy: FE-C control frames only, with session-relative timing. No addresses, absolute timestamps, device name or unrelated traffic. FE-C control frames carry no personal data.
